name: GGZ op Orde
author: ggzoporde

sections.description:
Dutch mental health practices (GGZ) must publish their waiting times every month, together with the NZa text about waiting list mediation, their contracted health insurers, their quality statute (kwaliteitsstatuut) and their complaints procedure. GGZ op Orde is the panel where a practice keeps that information; this plugin shows it on the practice’s own WordPress website.

Safe by design

  • Your own WordPress server fetches the information and shows it as ordinary text in your page. Visitors load no scripts, fonts or trackers from us, and nothing about your visitors is sent to us.
  • The panel gets no access to your WordPress: no administrator account, no application password.
  • Everything the panel sends is filtered with WordPress’s own HTML filter (wp_kses) before it is shown, so it can only ever contain text, headings, lists, tables, links and small icons.
  • If the panel cannot be reached, your website keeps showing the last copy it fetched, with its own reference month.

How it works

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Settings, GGZ op Orde, and paste your connection code (koppelcode). You find it in the panel under “Op uw website”; the “Koppelcode invullen” button there fills it in for you.
  3. Click “Create the page Waiting times”, or add the block “GGZ op Orde wachttijden” or the shortcode [ggz_op_orde] to any page.

Changes you make in the panel appear on your website within 15 minutes. The information is available in Dutch, English and Turkish; the block and the shortcode ([ggz_op_orde taal="en"]) can choose a language per page.

Nederlands

Met deze plugin staan uw wachttijden, de verplichte NZa-tekst over wachtlijstbemiddeling, uw gecontracteerde zorgverzekeraars, uw kwaliteitsstatuut en uw klachtenregeling altijd actueel op uw eigen WordPress-website. Uw website haalt de gegevens zelf op uit het GGZ op Orde-panel en toont ze als gewone tekst. Er draait geen code van ons op uw website en het panel krijgt geen toegang tot uw WordPress.

The plugin needs a GGZ op Orde subscription: see ggzoporde.nl.

External services

This plugin connects to the GGZ op Orde panel (https://panel.ggzoporde.nl), run by ViaNova Praktijk, Eindhoven (KvK 99383438), to fetch the practice information that it shows.

  • What is sent: your connection code (koppelcode) and the chosen language, in the address https://panel.ggzoporde.nl/e/<koppelcode>?lang=<language>. WordPress also sends its standard request header, which contains your website address; the panel uses it to tell you in the panel that your website shows the information.
  • When: when a page with the block or shortcode is opened and the stored copy is older than 10 minutes, and when you open the plugin’s settings screen. Nothing about your visitors is sent.
  • Terms of use: https://ggzoporde.nl/voorwaarden/
  • Privacy statement: https://ggzoporde.nl/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins, Add New Plugin, search for “GGZ op Orde”, click Install Now and then Activate. Or upload the zip file from the panel under Plugins, Add New Plugin, Upload Plugin.
  2. Go to Settings, GGZ op Orde, enter your connection code and save.
  3. Click “Create the page Waiting times” and add the page to your menu.
sections.faq:
Where do I find my connection code?

In the GGZ op Orde panel, under “Op uw website”. The code is public: it only shows the information that your website shows anyway.

Does my website become slower?

No. The information is stored for 10 minutes, so most visits make no request to the panel at all. If the panel is slow or unreachable, the request stops after 5 seconds and the last stored copy is shown.

Can I change the colours?

The colour is the practice colour set in the panel. The layout uses its own CSS classes (.ggzw), which your theme can adjust.

What happens when my subscription ends?

The panel then publishes nothing for your connection code, and the plugin shows nothing to visitors. Logged-in editors see a short note.
